Award Dated 09.07.2019, Passed By The Ii-Addl. Senior Civil

At Raichur, In Eca No.332/2014 And Enhance The Award
Compensation Of Rs.7,44,270/-.
 This Appeal Coming On For Orders, This Day, The Court
Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of their son Bheemareddy in a motor vehicle accident dated 30.06.2011, appellants who are petitioners before the Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation have filed this appeal under Section 30(1) of the Workmen's Compensation Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short).

2. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Commissioner for Employees' Compensation ('Commissioner' for short).
3.
It is the case of the petitioners that they are the parents of deceased-Bheemareddy.
Respondent No.1 is working as Manager in Birla Plus Life Insurance Company.
He is the owner of Maruti Car bearing Reg.No.KA-36-M- 8260.
Deceased-Bheemareddy was employed as driver with respondent No.1 on monthly salary of Rs.6,000/- and batta.
On 30.06.2011, deceased-Bheemareddy was proceeding with respondentNo.1.
Deceased was driving the car.
After completing the work at Hindupur they left at 11:30 p.m. due to sudden failure of head lights, the car hit the cement concrete wall of the tollgate.
While both of them sustained grievous injuries, Bheemareddy died on the way to the hospital.
In respect of the said incident, Crime No.51/2011 was registered.
As parents of deceased-Bheemareddy, petitioners are entitled for compensation.
4. Since petitioners failed to take steps against respondent No.1, petition was dismissed against him.
5. Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement disputing that there exists relationship of employer and employee between respondent No.1 and deceased.
Deceased was not possessing a valid driving licence and as such respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify respondent No.1 and sought for dismissal of petition.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Commissioner framed necessary issues.
7. To prove their case, petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW-1 and Ex.P1 to 9 are marked.
8. Respondent No.2 has not led any oral or documentary evidence on its behalf.

sentences.text: After considering the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, the Commissioner partly allowed the petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.6,55,730/- with interest at 12% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

10. During the course of argument, learned counsel for petitioners submitted that the commissioner has erred in taking the income of the deceased as Rs.6,000/- instead of Rs.10,000/- and thereby reducing the compensation.

11. The appeal is admitted on the following substantial questions of law:
"Whether the Commissioner has committed an error in taking the monthly wages of deceased at Rs.6,000/- as driver in view of the amendment made to Section 4(1-B) of the Workmen's Compensation Act by way f amending Act 45 of 2009?"

12. Heard arguments and perused the records.
13.

Admittedly, respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award and thereby findings of the Commissioner that deceased died on account of personal injuries sustained by him in an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment with respondent No.1 and the petitioners are his legal representatives and respondent Nos.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are liable to pay the compensation with interest at 12% p.a. has become final.
14. It is relevant to note that the accident is dated 30.06.2011.

In the claim petition, the petitioners have pleaded that the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month including batta i.e. Rs.6,000/-
p.m. and also batta.
However, they have failed to prove the exact income of the deceased.

Since the Commissioner has dismissed the petition as against respondent No.1 for petitioners having failed to take steps against him, there was no occasion for respondent No.1 also to lead evidence to prove the wages paid by him to the deceased.
Therefore, the Commissioner has considered his income as Rs.6,000/- and based on 50% of it calculated the compensation.

15. However, Section 4 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 deals with the criteria for calculating the compensation in case of death or permanent total disability or permanent partial disability/temporary disability, etc.

Section 4(1)(b) provides that the Central Government may by Notification in the official Gazette specify, for the purposes of sub-section (1), such monthly wages in relation to an employee as may be considered necessary.

As per this provision, with effect from 31.05.2010 vide Order No.S.O 1258(E) dated 31.05.2010, the Central Government has specified for the purpose of sub-section (1), the monthly wages as Rs.8,000/-.
Based on it, the petitioners are claiming that the wages should be taken at Rs.8,000/- instead of Rs.6,000/-.

16. Earlier Explanation-II to Section 4 provided that where the monthly wages of workman exceeds Rs.4,000/-, his monthly wages for the purposes of Clause (a) & (b) shall be deemed to be Rs.4,000/-
only.
In other words even where the monthly income of the workman exceeded Rs.4,000/- as per Explanation-II it was required to be limited to Rs.4,000/- and compensation was to be determined.
However, by Act 45 of 2009 Explanation-II is omitted.

In other words after the omission of Sri. Hanumanthareddy And Anr vs K. Sridhar And Anr on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72518259/
3 Explanation- II, the minimum wages which is required to be taken into consideration is as fixed by the Central Government under Section 4(1)(b).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the parties are able to establish that the wages received by the workman exceeded the amount specified by the Central Government, the same may be considered or else it shall not be less than what is fixed by the Central Government under Section 4(1)(b).
Having regard to this provision, the Commissioner has erred in considering the minimum wages of deceased at Rs.6,000/-.

It ought to have taken the wages of deceased at Rs.8,000/-.
17.
As per the material placed on record at the time of accident deceased was aged 25 years.
Therefore, rightly the Commissioner has taken the appropriate factor for calculating the compensation as 216.91.

Out of the wages of Rs.8,000/- 50% is required to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and remaining 50% is to be taken into consideration for calculating the compensation.

50% of Rs.8,000/- comes to Rs.4,000/- and when it is multiplied by appropriate factor i.e. 216.91, the compensation works out to Rs.8,67,640/-
i.e 4000 x 216.91 = 8,67,640/-.
18.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.8,67,640/- as against Rs.6,50,730/- granted by the Commissioner..
19. As per Section 4(4) petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses as allowed by the Commissioner.
Thus, in all the petitioners are entitled total compensation in a sum of Rs.8,72,640/-.
Accordingly, the 1st substantial question of law is answered in the Affirmative.

20. Since respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, it is liable to indemnify the owner i.e., respondent No.1 and as such respondent No.2 is liable to pay the enhanced compensation within a period of 30 days, failing which it is liable to pay the same together with simple interest at 12% p.a. after expiry of 30 days from the date of this order.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.8,72,640/- as against Rs.6,55,730/-
granted by the Commissioner.

(iii) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of 30 days from the date of this order, failing which, it is liable to pay simple interest at 12% per annum on the enhanced compensation, after the expiry of 30 days.
(iv) The registry shall send a copy of this order to the Commissioner.
